Directional whip-pan motion-blur cut

I wanted to know if one ElementGL canvas can whip-pan between two live HTML views with 16-tap directional blur, RGB fringe and a damped overshoot spring while keeping buttons and inputs clickable at rest. Tap a cut direction, swipe across the stage or scrub from 0% to 100%.

Show the code Dual drawable views, directional blur shader, spring curve and fallbacks
  1. Two live scenes inside one drawable canvas. #wp-scene-a (warm Studio Storyboard) and #wp-scene-b (dark indigo Timeline Sequence) sit inside <canvas id="wp-canvas" content="drawable" layoutsubtree>.
  2. Bell-curve velocity, damped overshoot spring and hit-box sync. stepWhipCut(..., tMs) drives the overshoot landing, whipBellVelocity() peaks at 50%, and syncSceneGeometry() moves the settled view into place while parking the other view offstage with inert.
  3. 16-tap directional velocity blur and RGB fringe shader. WHIP_FRAG samples both textures across the moving shutter vector uPanDir with red and blue channel offsets proportional to velocity and Blur px.
  4. Premultiplied alpha uploads, 2D fallback and context recovery. Sets UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL = true on creation and restore, calls stage.begin() before stage.upload() inside paint, and falls back to 5-argument drawElementImage() or #plain-host.

How it works

Both views live inside one <canvas id="wp-canvas" content="drawable" layoutsubtree> managed by a single ElementGL WebGL 2 context from /lib/element-gl.js. On creation and inside onRestored, the page turns on gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL, true) so badges and input borders keep clean anti-aliased edges. Inside the paint handler, hasPainted unlocks uploads and stage.begin() sizes the backing buffer before stage.upload() updates whichever scene changed.

During a cut or manual scrub, stepWhipCut(anim, tMs, reducedMotion) drives progress across a 480 ms S-curve with a damped overshoot spring landing (about 2.6% past the stop before rebounding to rest). whipBellVelocity() follows a raised sine bell curve that starts at 0, peaks at 1.0 around 50%, and returns to 0 when settled. In WHIP_FRAG, once velocity times Blur px exceeds 0.15 px, the shader integrates 16 directional taps along uPanDir across both the trailing half of Scene A and the entering half of Scene B while splitting red and blue channels along the pan axis for a subtle velocity fringe. At 0% and 100% rest, it drops to a single direct texture fetch so controls and text stay razor-sharp.

At rest, syncSceneGeometry() calibrates CSS-to-canvas units with geometryUnit(), places the settled scene over the canvas via updateElementGeometry(), moves the hidden scene to OFFSTAGE with inert = true, and flips data-hit-tick to clear Chromium's hit-test cache. The stage disables native drag selection with user-select: none plus a selectstart guard while keeping user-select: text on both title inputs. Idle preview cuts pause on IntersectionObserver, document.hidden, any touch or scrub, and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. When WebGL 2 isn't available or ?route=2d is set, a 5-argument drawElementImage() pass draws the moving frames; on webglcontextlost, ?route=plain or missing API support, both scenes move into #plain-host as plain HTML.

Live checks

These checks run on isolated fixtures inside testStage() and wait for a tap so opening the page doesn't allocate extra WebGL contexts or move focus.

StatusCheckDetail

Findings

  • Measured in HeadlessChrome/160.0.0.0 on 2026-11-27 (412 px wide, DPR 2.625, with CanvasDrawElement enabled): all 6 live checks pass with 0 console errors, scrollWidth === 412, a 945×893 backing store (0.844 MP, 6.75 MB initial, 12.18 MB peak), glPeak = 2, openSnapshots = 0, unaskedReads = 0 and wrongDraws = 0.
  • At 50% midpoint under Left blur (48 px), trailing edge luminance smeared from 255 at 0% rest down to 177 on mobile (185 at 960 px desktop) with a 1.026 overshoot peak from stepWhipCut(). Reversing axes swapped smear cleanly: Left gave H=97 vs V=12 and Up gave V=84 vs H=12.
  • Real CDP clicks and text entry hit View A at 0% (Take #1 incremented to Take #2; #wp-title-a updated to STUDIO REEL · OPENING EDITED) and View B at 100% (Marker #1 incremented to Marker #2; #wp-title-b updated to TIMELINE SEQ 04 · WHIP LIVE), and a touch swipe across the timeline track returned cleanly to 0%.
  • With ?route=2d, the 5-argument drawElementImage() fallback ran with wrongDraws = 0. With ?route=plain or --disable-blink-features=CanvasDrawElement, both scenes moved into #plain-host (inert = false, scrollWidth = 412). Under emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, idle preview stayed paused and clicking Up snapped straight to 100% with vel = 0%.
  • Running /lib/a11y-audit.js at 960×800 with tab focus emulation enabled passed 9 checks (calm, blank, dom, hit, ghost, focus 6/6, names 6/6, sharp, motion) with 0 failures and 1 warning (zoom, because ElementGL.#syncSize() doesn't multiply backing pixels by currentCSSZoom).
  • npm run check:jank, node tools/draw-size/audit.mjs, real Chrome 159 on Android hardware and social.jpg capture are not verified yet.
